id: GB-04 measure <handoff> and locate in a non-ASCII checkout under Git Bash's perl
note: Sitting 4, P4 (RF-7 c7 and AT-GR-03-gsd-bytes-pure-cwd on the PC): measure <handoff> with a gsd line in a checkout whose path is not ASCII ended perl with 'Out of memory!' before any output. skills gitfacts decodes git's drive-form toplevel (C:/.../rëpo) to characters, and util::root_form gave that flagged string to Cygwin::win_to_posix_path. The sub now gets bytes and ASCII only (util::_drive_posix). FakeXS.pm, loaded by the perl first on PATH, stands in for the real sub with no STORE_TEST_CYGDRIVE seam (C: reads as $TMP/cyg/c) and ends perl as the PC did: on a flagged string (FAKE_XS_ABORT=flagged) or on any non-ASCII input (nonascii, the other outcome of the PC probe). A git first on PATH prints $TMP/cyg/c/... as C:/....

setup.script:
out=$(PATH=${PATH#*:} git "$@"); rc=$?
[ -n "$out" ] && printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed 's#/[^ ]*/cyg/c/#C:/#g'
exit $rc
